newsitem.title: JAPAN: Recent Japan indicators show encouraging signs - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Recent Japan indicators show encouraging signs - BOJ.

text.p: An increasing number of recently released economic indicators have shown somewhat encouraging signs of the firmness of Japan's economic recovery, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said on Friday in its monthly economic review.

This is a statement of fact, and the central bank has not changed its basic assessment of the economy in its report, Shosaku Murayama, deputy director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, told reporters.
The report said a moderate economic recovery was continuing in Japan.
It also said the decline in Japan's net exports has paused, and that personal consumption continues to rise moderately.
Inventories are, on the whole, within appropriate levels, although those of some items are still somewhat excessive, it said.
Murayama also said that he did not have a clear outlook for the future.
"There are still some indicators which show weakness, so we would like to continue to take the overall situation into account in making our assessment," he said.
